requiredBehaviors.behavior: flag denominator, exposure or source-coverage limitations as evidence gaps and keep a trend hypothesis distinct from a confirmed trend
requiredBehaviors.evidence: The skill requires source coverage, denominator/exposure and data-quality review before trend claims and preserves trend hypotheses as hypotheses when evidence is incomplete.

requiredBehaviors.behavior: escalate the potentially time-critical case immediately to the specialist instead of waiting for periodic PMS or management review
requiredBehaviors.evidence: The time-critical action principle and Specialist Routing section require immediate specialist escalation independent of PMS or management-review cadence.

requiredBehaviors.behavior: keep no-events, no-signal, no-data and not-reviewed states distinct in the management-review input
requiredBehaviors.evidence: The PMS review and management-review handoff explicitly preserve separate no-events, no-signal, no-data and not-reviewed states.

forbiddenBehaviors.behavior: declare a statistical trend from increasing absolute counts alone
forbiddenBehaviors.evidence: The core principle A count is not a rate prevents absolute counts from becoming an automatic trend conclusion.

forbiddenBehaviors.behavior: invent a complaint-rate threshold or denominator to make the data appear complete
forbiddenBehaviors.evidence: Missing denominators and coverage remain evidence gaps and universal thresholds are explicitly rejected.

forbiddenBehaviors.behavior: defer a potentially reportable case until the next management review
forbiddenBehaviors.evidence: Time-critical regulatory actions bypass governance cadence and start immediately with the responsible specialist.
